To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CD18 of deer, elk, and bison were cloned and compared with other ruminants, and non-ruminant CD18.
the full-length cDNAs of CD18 from bison, white tailed deer, and elk have been cloned.
the cDNAs encoding bison, deer (white-tailed deer and mule deer) and elk CD18 were cloned and characterized, and that these CD18s are highly conserved among the ruminants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cloning and characterization, for the first time, of CD18 from three species of ruminants.
the cloning and characterization CD18 of bighorn sheep, elk and deer.
the cloning of bison, elk, and deer CD18 and comparison of their cDNA with that from other species.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CD18 of ruminant species is more similar to each other than CD18 of non-ruminant species.
CD18 of ruminants is most closely related among the same species while CD18 of non-ruminant species is most closely related between different species.
CD18 of deer, elk, and bison are more closely related phylogenetically to each other than to that of other raminants.
